reply: Watch out for the tram lines at the corner. They're slippery when wet.
transferCue: Tell a new colleague what to check in customer emails.
transferReply: Watch out for orders with a different billing and delivery address.
frame: Watch out for something / watch out!
nuance: Inseparable: watch out for it. Watch out! alone is an urgent warning. Look out for means the same, and can also mean take care of someone.
contrast: Watch out for warns about danger; look out for can also mean try to notice or protect someone.

exampleTranslations.Watch out for the tram lines at the corn: 角の路面電車のレールに気をつけて。濡れると滑るから。
exampleTranslations.Watch out for orders with a different bi: 請求先と配送先の住所が違う注文には注意して。

nuanceJapanese: 分離しない：watch out for it。Watch out! だけなら差し迫った警告。look out for も同じ意味で、人を気にかける意味にもなる。
contrastJapanese: watch out for は危険への注意。look out for は見つけようとする、あるいは人を守る意味にもなる。

meaning: Continue to support someone in a difficult time, or keep to a decision.
easyEnglish: Continue to support someone in a difficult time, or keep to a decision.
japanese: 困難なときも支え続ける。決めたことを守る。
cue: Describe how your friends reacted when you lost your job.
reply: They stuck by me the whole time. Someone called every day.
transferCue: A manager is asked to change a decision under pressure. Describe their answer.
transferReply: She stuck by her decision and explained the reasons again.
frame: Stick by someone / stick by a decision
nuance: Inseparable: stick by her. Stick is irregular: stuck. Stand by means the same for people; stick to is used for rules and plans.
contrast: Stick by supports a person or holds a decision; stick with keeps doing something.

exampleTranslations.They stuck by me the whole time. Someone: ずっと支えてくれた。誰かが毎日電話をくれたんだ。
exampleTranslations.She stuck by her decision and explained: 彼女は決定を変えず、理由をもう一度説明した。

nuanceJapanese: 分離しない：stick by her。stick は不規則で stuck。stand by は人について同じ意味。stick to は規則や計画に使う。
contrastJapanese: stick by は人を支える、または決定を曲げないこと。stick with は何かを続けること。

meaning: Stop letting something upset or block you, or manage to pass an obstacle.
easyEnglish: Stop letting something upset or block you, or manage to pass an obstacle.
japanese: 気持ちの上で乗り越える。障害を通り抜ける。
cue: A friend can't stop thinking about a rude comment. Respond.
reply: I know it stung, but try to get past it. He was having a bad day.
transferCue: Explain a difficulty with a job application.
transferReply: I never got past the first interview, so I don't know what they wanted.
frame: Get past something / can't get past the fact that…
nuance: Inseparable: get past it. Often negative: I can't get past what she said. Literal use is also common: we couldn't get past the roadworks.
contrast: Get past stops a thought from blocking you; get over recovers from an upset.

傷ついたのはわかるけど、乗り越えてみて。彼は機嫌の悪い日だったんだよ。
exampleTranslations.I never got past the first interview, so: 一次面接を通ったことがないから、何を求められていたのかわからない。

nuanceJapanese: 分離しない：get past it。否定で使うことが多い：I can't get past what she said。文字どおりの意味もよく使う：we couldn't get past the roadworks。
contrastJapanese: get past は考えが妨げになるのをやめること。get over は動揺から立ち直ること。

meaning: Believe that someone is capable of doing something bad or surprising.
easyEnglish: Believe that someone is capable of doing something bad or surprising.
japanese: 〜ならやりかねないと思う。
cue: A colleague suspects the new manager will cancel the bonus. Give your view.
reply: I wouldn't put it past him. He cut the travel budget in his first week.
transferCue: Your friend jokes that your cat opened the fridge. Respond.
transferReply: Honestly, I wouldn't put it past her. She has learned to open doors.
frame: Not put it past someone to do something / I wouldn't put it past her
nuance: Almost always negative with would: I wouldn't put it past him. The it stays fixed between put and past, and a following verb takes to: I wouldn't put it past them to cancel.

exampleTranslations.I wouldn't put it past him. He cut the t: 彼ならやりかねない。最初の週に出張予算を削った人だから。
exampleTranslations.Honestly, I wouldn't put it past her. Sh: 正直、あの子ならやりかねない。ドアの開け方を覚えたから。

nuanceJapanese: ほぼ常に would と否定で使う：I wouldn't put it past him。it は put と past の間に固定で、後ろに動詞が続くときは to：I wouldn't put it past them to cancel。

meaning: Make someone or something different from and better than others.
easyEnglish: Make someone or something different from and better than others.
japanese: 他と際立たせる。
cue: Explain why you chose one candidate over several strong ones.
reply: Her calm under pressure set her apart from the other candidates.
transferCue: Describe what makes your favourite café different.
transferReply: What sets it apart is the owner, who remembers everyone's order.
frame: Set someone apart from others / what sets it apart is…
nuance: Separable, usually with the object between: set her apart. Add from for the group: set apart from the rest. Often positive; a separate sense means reserve time or money.
contrast: Set apart makes something stand out; stand out is what the thing itself does.

exampleTranslations.Her calm under pressure set her apart fr: プレッシャーの中での落ち着きが、彼女を他の候補者から際立たせた。
exampleTranslations.What sets it apart is the owner, who rem: あの店を特別にしているのは、全員の注文を覚えている店主だ。

nuanceJapanese: 分離でき、たいてい目的語を間に置く：set her apart。比較対象は from で示す：set apart from the rest。多くは好意的な意味。別の意味で、時間やお金を取っておくこともある。
contrastJapanese: set apart は何かを際立たせること。stand out はそのもの自体が目立つこと。

meaning: Separate people or things that are together, or criticize something in detail.
easyEnglish: Separate people or things that are together, or criticize something in detail.
japanese: 引き離す。細かく批判する。
cue: Two children are fighting over a toy. Describe what you did.
reply: I had to pull them apart before someone got hurt.
transferCue: Describe how a reviewer treated your draft.
transferReply: She pulled the argument apart paragraph by paragraph, but her notes were fair.
frame: Pull people apart / pull an argument apart
nuance: Separable: pull them apart. With people it is physical separation; with a plan or piece of writing it means find every weakness. Tear apart is stronger and more emotional.
contrast: Pull apart separates or dissects; fall apart is what a thing does when it breaks by itself.

exampleTranslations.I had to pull them apart before someone: 誰かがけがをする前に、二人を引き離さなければならなかった。
exampleTranslations.She pulled the argument apart paragraph: 彼女は段落ごとに論旨を細かく崩していったが、指摘は公平だった。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：pull them apart。人なら物理的に引き離すこと、計画や文章ならあらゆる弱点を見つけること。tear apart はより強く感情的。
contrastJapanese: pull apart は引き離す、または細かく分析すること。fall apart は物が自然に壊れること。

meaning: Make or prepare something quickly and without much care.
easyEnglish: Make or prepare something quickly and without much care.
japanese: 手早く間に合わせで作る。
cue: Unexpected guests arrive at dinner time. Reassure your partner.
reply: I can throw together a pasta with what's in the fridge.
transferCue: Explain why a presentation looked rough.
transferReply: We threw it together the night before, so the slides don't match.
frame: Throw something together / throw a meal together
nuance: Separable: throw it together. Suggests speed and improvisation rather than poor quality. People can also be thrown together by circumstances: we were thrown together on a training course.
contrast: Throw together is fast and improvised; put together is careful assembly.

exampleTranslations.I can throw together a pasta with what's: 冷蔵庫にあるものでパスタをさっと作れるよ。
exampleTranslations.We threw it together the night before, s: 前の晩に急いでまとめたから、スライドの体裁がそろっていない。

nuanceJapanese: 分離できる：throw it together。速さと即興を表し、必ずしも質が低いわけではない。人が状況によって一緒になることも表す：we were thrown together on a training course。
contrastJapanese: throw together は手早い即興。put together は丁寧に組み立てること。

meaning: Join with other people in order to achieve something together.
easyEnglish: Join with other people in order to achieve something together.
japanese: 力を合わせるために団結する。
cue: Describe how your street dealt with a noisy construction site.
reply: The neighbours banded together and asked the council for quiet hours.
transferCue: Encourage colleagues to respond to a policy as a group.
transferReply: If we band together, they will have to listen. One complaint is easy to ignore.
frame: Band together / band together to do something / band together against something
nuance: No object. Usually a group with a shared problem or goal; add against for an opponent. Join forces means the same in more formal writing.
contrast: Band together is people uniting for a purpose; get together is simply meeting.

exampleTranslations.The neighbours banded together and asked: 近所の人たちが団結して、議会に静かな時間帯を設けるよう求めた。
exampleTranslations.If we band together, they will have to l: みんなで団結すれば、向こうも聞かざるを得ない。苦情ひとつなら無視されやすい。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。共通の問題や目標を持つ集団が主語で、相手は against で示す。join forces はよりフォーマルな書き言葉で同じ意味。
contrastJapanese: band together は目的のために人が団結すること。get together は単に集まること。

meaning: Make fast progress or continue with determination.
easyEnglish: Make fast progress or continue with determination.
japanese: 力強く前進する。
cue: Give a short status update on a project that is going well.
reply: The design team is forging ahead. Two screens are already in testing.
transferCue: Describe a friend who kept studying while others quit.
transferReply: Most of the class dropped out, but she forged ahead and passed in June.
frame: Forge ahead / forge ahead with something
nuance: No object; add with for the project: forge ahead with the plan. Forge is pronounced with a soft g, like large. Slightly literary and positive.
contrast: Forge ahead stresses energetic progress; press ahead stresses continuing despite objections.

exampleTranslations.The design team is forging ahead. Two sc: デザインチームは順調に前進しています。すでに2画面がテストに入りました。
exampleTranslations.Most of the class dropped out, but she f: クラスの大半は脱落したけど、彼女は前に進み続けて6月に合格した。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。対象は with で示す：forge ahead with the plan。forge の g は large と同じやわらかい音。やや文学的で前向きな表現。
contrastJapanese: forge ahead は力強い前進を強調する。press ahead は反対があっても続けることを強調する。

meaning: Move in front of others in a race, competition or market.
easyEnglish: Move in front of others in a race, competition or market.
japanese: 競争相手を抜いて先に出る。
cue: Describe how the sales race between two teams changed in March.
reply: Our team pulled ahead in March after the new pricing went live.
transferCue: Talk about a cycling race you watched.
transferReply: She pulled ahead on the final climb and won by twenty seconds.
frame: Pull ahead / pull ahead of someone
nuance: No object; add of for the rival: pull ahead of the competition. From racing, now common in business and sport. Get ahead is about personal success rather than a race.
contrast: Pull ahead overtakes a rival; get ahead advances in life or a career.

exampleTranslations.Our team pulled ahead in March after the: 新しい価格が始まった3月に、うちのチームが先に出た。
exampleTranslations.She pulled ahead on the final climb and: 彼女は最後の登りで抜け出し、20秒差で勝った。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語なし。相手は of で示す：pull ahead of the competition。レース由来で、今はビジネスやスポーツでよく使う。get ahead は競争ではなく個人の成功について。
contrastJapanese: pull ahead は競争相手を抜くこと。get ahead は人生や仕事で先に進むこと。

meaning: Continue moving or working towards a goal with effort.
easyEnglish: Continue moving or working towards a goal with effort.
japanese: 努力して前に進める。
cue: The first version of a feature got mixed feedback. Tell the team the plan.
reply: The feedback is useful, but we'll push forward with the release and fix the rough edges next sprint.
transferCue: Describe a hike in bad weather.
transferReply: The rain got heavier, but we pushed forward to the hut.
frame: Push forward / push forward with something
nuance: No object in this sense; add with for the plan. Push something forward can also mean move a date or item earlier or higher in priority. Push ahead and press ahead are close.
contrast: Push forward keeps moving despite effort; move on leaves one thing to start the next.

exampleTranslations.The feedback is useful, but we'll push f: フィードバックは役に立つけど、リリースは進めて、粗い部分は次のスプリントで直します。
exampleTranslations.The rain got heavier, but we pushed forw: 雨は強くなったが、私たちは山小屋まで進み続けた。

nuanceJapanese: この意味では目的語なし。計画は with で示す。push something forward は日程や項目を前倒しする・優先度を上げる意味にもなる。push ahead や press ahead が近い。
contrastJapanese: push forward は努力して進み続けること。move on はひとつを終えて次に移ること。

meaning: Have a similar appearance to someone or something, or seem likely.
easyEnglish: Have a similar appearance to someone or something, or seem likely.
japanese: 〜に似ている。〜のようだ。
cue: A friend shows you a photo of their brother. React.
reply: He looks like you, especially the smile.
transferCue: Look at the sky and comment on the weather.
transferReply: It looks like rain. Let's take the umbrella.
frame: Look like someone / it looks like rain / it looks like + clause
nuance: Inseparable: look like her. Followed by a noun, or by a clause in speech: it looks like we're late. What does he look like? asks about appearance; what is he like? asks about character.
contrast: Look like is about appearance or likelihood; feel like is about wanting something.

君に似てるね。特に笑顔が。
exampleTranslations.It looks like rain. Let's take the umbre: 雨になりそう。傘を持っていこう。

nuanceJapanese: 分離しない：look like her。後ろには名詞、会話では節も続く：it looks like we're late。What does he look like? は外見、What is he like? は性格を尋ねる。
contrastJapanese: look like は外見や見込みについて。feel like は何かをしたい気持ちについて。

meaning: A gain you already have is worth more than a bigger one you might never get.
easyEnglish: A gain you already have is worth more than a bigger one you might never get.
japanese: 手元にある確かなものは、当てにならない大きな望みより価値がある。
cue: A friend wants to turn down a firm job offer to wait for a better one. Advise caution.
reply: A bird in the hand is worth a lot right now. You could accept and keep looking quietly.
transferCue: Explain why you took the smaller of two possible deals.
transferReply: I took the offer because a bird in the hand felt safer than a promise.
frame: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
nuance: Usually shortened in speech; the full proverb is a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush. It advises caution, so it can sound discouraging if the other person is excited.

exampleTranslations.A bird in the hand is worth a lot right: 今は、確実に手にしているもののほうが価値があります。受けておいて、静かに探し続けることもできます。
exampleTranslations.I took the offer because a bird in the h: 約束より確実なもののほうが安心だったので、その条件を受けました。

nuanceJapanese: 会話では短く言うことが多く、完全な形は a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush。慎重さを勧める表現なので、相手が乗り気なときは水を差すように響くことがある。

meaning: Everything possible, with nothing left out.
easyEnglish: Everything possible, with nothing left out.
japanese: 一切合切。できることを全部。
cue: A friend asks how elaborate your birthday dinner was. It was very elaborate.
reply: Candles, three courses, a playlist — the whole nine yards.
transferCue: Describe how thoroughly you prepared for a presentation.
transferReply: I went the whole nine yards: slides, handouts and a rehearsal.
frame: The whole nine yards / go the whole nine yards
nuance: Informal and mostly American. Often ends a list as a summary, after a dash or a pause.

exampleTranslations.Candles, three courses, a playlist — the: キャンドルに3品のコース、プレイリストまで、全部そろえました。
exampleTranslations.I went the whole nine yards: slides, han: スライドも資料もリハーサルも、できることは全部やりました。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、主にアメリカ英語。列挙のあとにダッシュや間をおいて、まとめとして置くことが多い。

meaning: Stop something that is failing before it costs you more.
easyEnglish: Stop something that is failing before it costs you more.
japanese: これ以上の損を防ぐために、早めに手を引く。
cue: A side project has cost money for months with no results. Suggest stopping.
reply: I think we should cut our losses and close it before the next invoice.
transferCue: Explain why you left a course you had already paid for.
transferReply: I decided to cut my losses rather than spend another term on it.
frame: Cut your losses and do something
nuance: The possessive changes with the subject: cut my losses, cut our losses. It accepts that money or time is already gone and protects what is left.

exampleTranslations.I think we should cut our losses and clo: 次の請求が来る前に、損を広げないよう畳んだほうがいいと思います。
exampleTranslations.I decided to cut my losses rather than s: もう1学期かけるより、そこで区切りをつけることにしました。

nuanceJapanese: 主語に合わせて所有格が変わる：cut my losses、cut our losses。すでに失ったものは受け入れ、残りを守るという発想の表現。

meaning: Do many difficult or annoying things to get something.
easyEnglish: Do many difficult or annoying things to get something.
japanese: 目的のために、面倒な手続きをいくつもこなす。
cue: A friend asks how hard it was to get your visa. It took many steps.
reply: I had to jump through hoops for months before it was approved.
transferCue: Warn a colleague about an approval process.
transferReply: Be ready to jump through hoops. Finance asks for three signatures.
frame: Jump through hoops to do something
nuance: Usually complains about the process rather than the person. Make somebody jump through hoops blames whoever set the rules.

exampleTranslations.I had to jump through hoops for months b: 承認されるまで、何か月も面倒な手続きを踏み続けました。
exampleTranslations.Be ready to jump through hoops. Finance: 面倒な手続きは覚悟してください。経理は署名を3つ求めます。

nuanceJapanese: 人ではなく手続きへの不満を表すことが多い。make somebody jump through hoops と言えば、その仕組みを作った側を責める言い方になる。

phrase: on the tip of my tongue
meaning: Almost remembered, but not quite said yet.
easyEnglish: Almost remembered, but not quite said yet.
japanese: 喉まで出かかっているのに、思い出せない。
cue: Someone asks the name of a restaurant you both liked. You cannot recall it.
reply: It's on the tip of my tongue. Something with a bird in the name.
transferCue: Apologise for forgetting a colleague's name mid-introduction.
transferReply: Sorry — your surname was on the tip of my tongue a second ago.
frame: It's on the tip of my tongue
nuance: The possessive follows the person who is trying to remember. Usually said while still searching, not after giving up.
aliases: on the tip of your tongue
on the tip of her tongue
on the tip of his tongue

exampleTranslations.It's on the tip of my tongue. Something: 喉まで出かかっています。鳥の名前が入っていたような。
exampleTranslations.Sorry — your surname was on the tip of m: すみません、さっきまで名字が出かかっていたんです。

nuanceJapanese: 思い出そうとしている人に合わせて所有格が変わる。あきらめたあとではなく、まだ探している最中に言うのがふつう。

meaning: Blame or sacrifice someone to protect yourself.
easyEnglish: Blame or sacrifice someone to protect yourself.
japanese: 自分を守るために、他人に責任を押しつける。
cue: A teammate named you alone when a shared mistake was raised. Describe it to a friend.
reply: He threw me under the bus even though we agreed on it together.
transferCue: Reassure a nervous junior colleague before a review meeting.
transferReply: I'm not going to throw you under the bus. We decided this as a team.
frame: Throw someone under the bus
nuance: Informal and strongly critical. The person named between throw and under is the one being blamed.

exampleTranslations.He threw me under the bus even though we: 一緒に決めたことなのに、彼は私だけのせいにしました。
exampleTranslations.I'm not going to throw you under the bus: あなたに責任を押しつけたりしません。チームで決めたことです。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた言い方で、強い非難を含む。throw と under のあいだに来る人が、責任を押しつけられる側。

meaning: Misunderstand each other because of confused information.
easyEnglish: Misunderstand each other because of confused information.
japanese: 話が食い違って、互いに誤解する。
cue: You and a friend went to different cafés at the same time. Explain lightly.
reply: I think we got our wires crossed. I was waiting at the other branch.
transferCue: Apologise to a colleague for a scheduling mix-up.
transferReply: Sorry, we must have got our wires crossed about the start time.
frame: Get your wires crossed about something
nuance: Blames the confusion rather than a person, which makes it a gentle way to raise a mix-up. British English also says get your lines crossed.

exampleTranslations.I think we got our wires crossed. I was: 行き違いだったみたいです。私はもう一方の店で待っていました。
exampleTranslations.Sorry, we must have got our wires crosse: すみません、開始時刻について行き違いがあったようです。

nuanceJapanese: 人ではなく行き違いそのもののせいにするので、やわらかく指摘できる。イギリス英語では get your lines crossed とも言う。

phrase: the best thing since sliced bread
meaning: Something praised as extremely good or useful.
easyEnglish: Something praised as extremely good or useful.
japanese: これ以上ないほど素晴らしいもの。
cue: A friend keeps recommending an app. Describe their enthusiasm.
reply: She thinks that app is the best thing since sliced bread.
transferCue: Praise a small kitchen tool you bought.
transferReply: This little peeler is the best thing since sliced bread.
frame: Be the best thing since sliced bread
nuance: Informal and often lightly teasing. Said about another person's enthusiasm, it can sound sceptical.

exampleTranslations.She thinks that app is the best thing si: 彼女はそのアプリを、これ以上ないほどいいものだと思っています。
exampleTranslations.This little peeler is the best thing sin: この小さなピーラーは、本当に買ってよかったものです。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、からかいを含むことも多い。他人の熱中ぶりについて使うと、少し冷めた響きになる。

phrase: a chip off the old block
meaning: A child who is very like one of their parents.
easyEnglish: A child who is very like one of their parents.
japanese: 親にそっくりな子ども。
cue: A friend's son has started cooking exactly the way his father does. Comment warmly.
reply: He's a chip off the old block. He even tastes the sauce the same way.
transferCue: Describe how you resemble your mother.
transferReply: People say I'm a chip off the old block whenever I start organising things.
frame: Be a chip off the old block
nuance: Affectionate and informal, and traditionally about resembling a father, though it is now used for either parent.

exampleTranslations.He's a chip off the old block. He even t: お父さんそっくりですね。ソースの味見の仕方まで同じです。
exampleTranslations.People say I'm a chip off the old block: 何かを整理し始めると、母そっくりだと言われます。

nuanceJapanese: 親しみを込めたくだけた表現。もとは父親に似ている場合に使ったが、今はどちらの親にも使う。

meaning: Agree to forget a past disagreement.
easyEnglish: Agree to forget a past disagreement.
japanese: 過去のいざこざを水に流す。
cue: An old argument still sits between you and a cousin. Offer peace at a family dinner.
reply: Can we let bygones be bygones? I'd rather enjoy the evening.
transferCue: Describe how two colleagues moved past a conflict.
transferReply: They decided to let bygones be bygones and started sharing a desk again.
frame: Let bygones be bygones
nuance: Fixed wording; bygones does not change. It proposes moving on rather than settling who was right.

exampleTranslations.Can we let bygones be bygones? I'd rathe: もう水に流しませんか。今夜は楽しく過ごしたいです。
exampleTranslations.They decided to let bygones be bygones a: 二人は過去のことを水に流し、また同じ机を使うようになりました。

nuanceJapanese: 語形は固定で、bygones は変化しない。どちらが正しかったかを決めるのではなく、先へ進もうと提案する表現。

meaning: Take what is offered when you are in no position to ask for more.
easyEnglish: Take what is offered when you are in no position to ask for more.
japanese: もらう立場では、えり好みはできない。
cue: A friend complains that the free sofa is the wrong colour. Reply lightly.
reply: Beggars can't be choosers. It's free and it's comfortable.
transferCue: Accept a last-minute room that is smaller than you wanted.
transferReply: It's small, but beggars can't be choosers at this notice.
frame: Beggars can't be choosers
nuance: A set proverb, usually said about yourself or as light teasing. Said to someone in real need it sounds harsh.

exampleTranslations.Beggars can't be choosers. It's free and: もらう立場ではえり好みできません。無料で、座り心地もいいですよ。
exampleTranslations.It's small, but beggars can't be chooser: 狭いですが、この直前ではえり好みできません。

nuanceJapanese: 決まった形のことわざで、自分のことか、軽いからかいとして使うのがふつう。本当に困っている人に向けると冷たく響く。

meaning: Make the best impression or effort you can.
easyEnglish: Make the best impression or effort you can.
japanese: できるかぎりよい印象を与えようと努める。
cue: A friend is nervous before an interview. Encourage them.
reply: Just put your best foot forward. They already liked your application.
transferCue: Describe how your team approached a first client meeting.
transferReply: We put our best foot forward and brought a working prototype.
frame: Put your best foot forward
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It is about presenting yourself well, not about winning.

exampleTranslations.Just put your best foot forward. They al: できるかぎりの自分を見せればいいですよ。応募書類の時点で好印象です。
exampleTranslations.We put our best foot forward and brought: 私たちは全力で臨み、動く試作品を持っていきました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。勝つことではなく、自分をよく見せることに焦点がある表現。

meaning: Fail, break down, or come to an end.
easyEnglish: Fail, break down, or come to an end.
japanese: だめになる。壊れて使えなくなる。
cue: Your old printer has finally stopped working. Tell a housemate.
reply: The printer has finally bitten the dust. We need a new one.
transferCue: Describe what happened to a plan that ran out of money.
transferReply: The project bit the dust when the funding stopped.
frame: Something bites the dust
nuance: Informal and a little dramatic. Used about things and plans; about people it means die, so avoid it there.

プリンターがとうとう壊れました。新しいのが必要です。
exampleTranslations.The project bit the dust when the fundin: 資金が止まった時点で、その企画は立ち消えになりました。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた、やや大げさな言い方。物や計画について使う。人について使うと「死ぬ」の意味になるので避ける。

meaning: Treat something as far more serious than it is.
easyEnglish: Treat something as far more serious than it is.
japanese: 実際より大げさに騒ぎ立てる。
cue: A small typo has turned into a long email thread. Calm the discussion.
reply: I think we're blowing things out of proportion. It's one line on page four.
transferCue: Admit that you overreacted to a friend's late reply.
transferReply: I blew it out of proportion. You were just busy.
frame: Blow something out of proportion
nuance: Often used about your own reaction as a way of stepping back. Aimed at someone else it can sound dismissive.

exampleTranslations.I think we're blowing things out of prop: 少し大げさになっている気がします。4ページ目の1行の話です。
exampleTranslations.I blew it out of proportion. You were ju: 私が大げさに受け取りました。あなたは忙しかっただけですね。

nuanceJapanese: 自分の反応を振り返って距離を取るときによく使う。相手に向けて言うと、軽くあしらう響きになることがある。

meaning: Do something in a completely new way.
easyEnglish: Do something in a completely new way.
japanese: これまでのやり方を破って、新しいことをする。
cue: A colleague proposes a format nobody in your field uses. Support it.
reply: It would break the mould, but that might be exactly what we need.
transferCue: Describe a musician who changed what their genre sounded like.
transferReply: Her first album broke the mould for that kind of music.
frame: Break the mould
nuance: Mould is British spelling and mold American; both are common. Usually positive, about originality rather than rule-breaking.

exampleTranslations.It would break the mould, but that might: これまでの型を破ることになりますが、まさにそれが必要なのかもしれません。
exampleTranslations.Her first album broke the mould for that: 彼女のファーストアルバムは、その種の音楽の常識を変えました。

nuanceJapanese: mould はイギリス式、mold はアメリカ式で、どちらもよく使う。規則破りというより独創性を指し、ふつうは肯定的。

meaning: By any means necessary.
easyEnglish: By any means necessary.
japanese: どんな手段を使ってでも。
cue: A deadline cannot move and the team is behind. State your resolve.
reply: We'll get it finished by Friday by hook or by crook.
transferCue: Describe how you reached a wedding despite cancelled trains.
transferReply: I got there by hook or by crook — two buses and a long walk.
frame: By hook or by crook
nuance: A fixed old phrase, slightly dramatic. It signals determination rather than genuinely dishonest methods.

exampleTranslations.We'll get it finished by Friday by hook: どんな手を使ってでも、金曜までに仕上げます。
exampleTranslations.I got there by hook or by crook — two bu: バス2本と長い徒歩で、なんとかたどり着きました。

nuanceJapanese: 形の決まった古い表現で、やや芝居がかった響き。実際に不正な手段を指すというより、強い決意を表す。

meaning: Say plainly what something really is.
easyEnglish: Say plainly what something really is.
japanese: 遠回しにせず、ありのままに言う。
cue: A friend keeps softening what was clearly a broken promise. Name it plainly.
reply: Let's call a spade a spade. He cancelled twice without telling you.
transferCue: Describe a manager known for direct feedback.
transferReply: She calls a spade a spade, so you always know where you stand.
frame: Call a spade a spade
nuance: Usually approving of plain speech. It can be used to justify bluntness, so a softer opener helps in sensitive moments.

exampleTranslations.Let's call a spade a spade. He cancelled: はっきり言いましょう。彼は連絡もなく2回断っています。
exampleTranslations.She calls a spade a spade, so you always: 彼女は率直に言うので、自分の立場がいつも分かります。

nuanceJapanese: 率直さを肯定する文脈で使うことが多い。歯に衣着せない物言いの言い訳にもなるので、デリケートな場面では前置きがあるとよい。

phrase: can't see the wood for the trees
meaning: Miss the overall situation because you are lost in details.
easyEnglish: Miss the overall situation because you are lost in details.
japanese: 細部にとらわれて、全体が見えなくなる。
cue: A colleague has spent a week on formatting and forgotten the argument. Suggest stepping back.
reply: I think you can't see the wood for the trees. What's the main point again?
transferCue: Explain why you asked someone outside the team to read a draft.
transferReply: After three months I can't see the wood for the trees, so I need fresh eyes.
frame: Can't see the wood for the trees
nuance: Wood is the British version and forest the American one. It describes being too close to the work, not carelessness.
aliases: can't see the forest for the trees

exampleTranslations.I think you can't see the wood for the t: 細部にとらわれて全体が見えていない気がします。主な論点は何でしたか。
exampleTranslations.After three months I can't see the wood: 3か月もやると全体が見えなくなるので、別の目が必要です。

nuanceJapanese: wood はイギリス式、forest はアメリカ式。不注意ではなく、対象に近づきすぎている状態を表す。

meaning: Not clear at all.
easyEnglish: Not clear at all.
japanese: さっぱり分からない。まったく明快でない。
cue: An instruction page has left you more confused. React to a friend.
reply: I read it twice and it's as clear as mud.
transferCue: Give honest feedback on a confusing diagram.
transferReply: The colours help, but the labels are as clear as mud.
frame: Be as clear as mud
nuance: Ironic: it means the opposite of clear. Light and informal, so it softens criticism of a document.

exampleTranslations.I read it twice and it's as clear as mud: 2回読みましたが、さっぱり分かりません。
exampleTranslations.The colours help, but the labels are as: 色は助けになりますが、ラベルはまるで分かりません。

nuanceJapanese: 皮肉で、clear の反対の意味になる。軽くくだけた言い方なので、資料への批判をやわらげられる。

meaning: Become less shy and more willing to talk to people.
easyEnglish: Become less shy and more willing to talk to people.
japanese: 人見知りが薄れて、打ち解けてくる。
cue: A quiet new colleague has started joining conversations. Mention it kindly.
reply: She's really come out of her shell since the team lunch.
transferCue: Describe your own first months in a new city.
transferReply: It took a year for me to come out of my shell here.
frame: Come out of your shell
nuance: The possessive follows the person. Warm and encouraging; it describes gradual change, not a single evening.

exampleTranslations.She's really come out of her shell since: チームの昼食以降、彼女はすっかり打ち解けました。
exampleTranslations.It took a year for me to come out of my: ここで打ち解けるまでに1年かかりました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格はその人に合わせる。温かく励ます響きで、一晩の変化ではなく少しずつの変化を表す。

meaning: Occur to you as a thought.
easyEnglish: Occur to you as a thought.
japanese: ふと頭に浮かぶ。
cue: Someone asks whether you ever considered moving abroad. You have, briefly.
reply: It has crossed my mind, but I've never looked into it seriously.
transferCue: Deny that you suspected a friend of anything.
transferReply: It never crossed my mind that you'd forgotten on purpose.
frame: It crossed my mind that…
nuance: The thought is the subject: it crossed my mind, not I crossed my mind. Often used with never to deny a suspicion.

japanese: 前提が違いすぎて、比べても意味がないものを比べる。
cue: Someone compares this year's figures with a period that had a sale. Object.
reply: That's comparing apples and oranges. One quarter had a promotion.
transferCue: Explain why two job offers are hard to rank.
transferReply: I'm comparing apples and oranges — one is salary, the other is time.
frame: Compare apples and oranges
nuance: Both and and with are used. It challenges the comparison itself rather than the conclusion.

exampleTranslations.That's comparing apples and oranges. One: それは前提が違う比較です。片方の四半期には販促がありました。
exampleTranslations.I'm comparing apples and oranges — one i: 比べにくいんです。片方は給与、もう片方は時間の話なので。

nuanceJapanese: and と with のどちらも使う。結論ではなく、比較そのものに異議を唱える表現。

meaning: Choose only the best or most convenient items.
easyEnglish: Choose only the best or most convenient items.
japanese: 都合のいいものだけを選び取る。
cue: A summary quotes only the positive survey answers. Point it out.
reply: The report seems to cherry-pick the comments that support the decision.
transferCue: Admit you only read part of a long document.
transferReply: I could only cherry-pick the sections about pricing, so ask me about those.
frame: Cherry-pick something
nuance: Written with a hyphen and normally used with a modal or after to, as cherry-pick. Usually critical about someone else's selection.

exampleTranslations.The report seems to cherry-pick the comm: その報告は、結論に合う意見だけを選んで引用しているように見えます。
exampleTranslations.I could only cherry-pick the sections ab: 価格の項目だけ拾い読みできたので、その部分なら答えられます。

nuanceJapanese: ハイフンでつないで書き、助動詞や to のあとで cherry-pick の形で使うのがふつう。他人の選び方について言うと批判的になることが多い。

meaning: Pretending to dislike something you could not have.
easyEnglish: Pretending to dislike something you could not have.
japanese: 手に入らなかったものを、負け惜しみでけなすこと。
cue: Someone who missed out now says the role was boring anyway. Comment.
reply: That sounds like sour grapes to me.
transferCue: Check your own reaction to a rejection.
transferReply: I don't want this to be sour grapes, but the brief was never clear.
frame: Be sour grapes
nuance: Uncountable and always plural in form. Saying it about someone is a direct accusation of insincerity.

それは負け惜しみに聞こえます。
exampleTranslations.I don't want this to be sour grapes, but: 負け惜しみにはしたくないのですが、依頼内容は最初から曖昧でした。

nuanceJapanese: 不可算だが形はつねに複数。人に向けて言うと、本心ではないと直接指摘することになる。

meaning: Look foolish because of something you said or did.
easyEnglish: Look foolish because of something you said or did.
japanese: 言ったことややったことで、恥をかく。
cue: A confident public prediction turned out wrong. Describe the result.
reply: We had egg on our face when the numbers came out.
transferCue: Advise caution before announcing something unconfirmed.
transferReply: Let's wait for confirmation. I'd rather not have egg on my face on Monday.
frame: Have egg on your face
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. It describes public embarrassment, usually after overconfidence.

exampleTranslations.We had egg on our face when the numbers: 数字が出たとき、私たちは恥をかきました。
exampleTranslations.Let's wait for confirmation. I'd rather: 確認を待ちましょう。月曜に恥をかきたくありません。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。自信過剰のあとに人前で恥をかくことを表す。

meaning: Have a long, relaxed conversation.
easyEnglish: Have a long, relaxed conversation.
japanese: のんびりと長話をする。
cue: You ran into a former colleague and talked for an hour. Describe it.
reply: We stood outside and chewed the fat for an hour.
transferCue: Invite a friend for an unhurried catch-up.
transferReply: Come over on Sunday and we can chew the fat.
frame: Chew the fat
nuance: Informal and friendly. It implies no agenda, so it does not fit a work meeting.

exampleTranslations.We stood outside and chewed the fat for: 外に立ったまま、1時間ほど長話をしました。
exampleTranslations.Come over on Sunday and we can chew the: 日曜に来てください。のんびり話しましょう。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた親しみのある表現。目的のない雑談を指すので、仕事の打ち合わせには合わない。

meaning: Good at your job and deserving respect.
easyEnglish: Good at your job and deserving respect.
japanese: その仕事にふさわしい、腕のある。
cue: Someone doubts that a professional would miss this detail. Reply.
reply: Any editor worth her salt would have caught that.
transferCue: Describe what you expect from a good guide.
transferReply: A guide worth his salt would know the back route.
frame: Any X worth your salt
nuance: Comes after the noun it describes, often with any: any teacher worth their salt. The possessive matches that noun.

exampleTranslations.Any editor worth her salt would have cau: 腕のある編集者なら、あれは見逃さなかったはずです。
exampleTranslations.A guide worth his salt would know the ba: 腕のあるガイドなら、裏道を知っているものです。

nuanceJapanese: 修飾する名詞のあとに置き、any と組み合わせることが多い。所有格はその名詞に合わせる。

meaning: An ordinary person who is honest and good.
easyEnglish: An ordinary person who is honest and good.
japanese: 飾らず誠実な、立派な人。
cue: A neighbour has quietly helped your family for years. Describe them.
reply: Mrs Aoki is the salt of the earth. She never mentions any of it.
transferCue: Describe the volunteers at a local shelter.
transferReply: The people who run it are the salt of the earth.
frame: Be the salt of the earth
nuance: Always with the and singular in form, even about several people. Warm and slightly formal praise.

exampleTranslations.Mrs Aoki is the salt of the earth. She n: 青木さんは誠実で立派な方です。そのことを口にしません。
exampleTranslations.The people who run it are the salt of th: あそこを運営している人たちは、本当に誠実な方々です。

nuanceJapanese: 複数の人についても、the を伴い単数の形のまま使う。温かく、やや改まったほめ言葉。

meaning: Feel annoyed with yourself for a mistake you could have avoided.
easyEnglish: Feel annoyed with yourself for a mistake you could have avoided.
japanese: 避けられたミスを悔やんで、自分に腹を立てる。
cue: You left the booking until the price doubled. React.
reply: I could kick myself for not booking in April.
transferCue: Comfort a friend who forgot to submit a form on time.
transferReply: Don't kick yourself. The deadline was buried in the email.
frame: Could kick myself for doing something
nuance: The reflexive follows the subject. Usually with could rather than the plain past, and about regret rather than real anger.

exampleTranslations.I could kick myself for not booking in A: 4月に予約しなかったことが、悔やんでも悔やみきれません。
exampleTranslations.Don't kick yourself. The deadline was bu: 自分を責めないでください。締め切りはメールの中に埋もれていました。

nuanceJapanese: 再帰代名詞は主語に合わせる。単純な過去形より could と一緒に使い、本当の怒りではなく後悔を表す。

meaning: Leave someone without the help they were relying on.
easyEnglish: Leave someone without the help they were relying on.
japanese: 頼りにしていた相手を、見捨てて困らせる。
cue: A supplier cancelled the day before your event. Describe the effect.
reply: They cancelled on Friday and left us high and dry.
transferCue: Promise a colleague you will not withdraw from a joint task.
transferReply: I won't leave you high and dry. I'll finish my half whatever happens.
frame: Leave someone high and dry
nuance: The person stranded goes between leave and high. It blames the person who withdrew, so it is a strong complaint.

exampleTranslations.They cancelled on Friday and left us hig: 先方は金曜に断ってきて、私たちは困り果てました。
exampleTranslations.I won't leave you high and dry. I'll fin: あなたを困らせたりしません。何があっても自分の分は仕上げます。

nuanceJapanese: 取り残された人は leave と high のあいだに置く。手を引いた側を責める、かなり強い言い方。

meaning: Listen sympathetically to someone.
easyEnglish: Listen sympathetically to someone.
japanese: 親身になって話を聞く。
cue: A colleague seems to be carrying something difficult. Offer support.
reply: If you ever want someone to lend an ear, I'm around at lunch.
transferCue: Thank a friend who listened without advising.
transferReply: Thanks for lending an ear last night. That was all I needed.
frame: Lend an ear to someone
nuance: Slightly formal and warm. To introduces the person, and it implies listening rather than giving advice.

exampleTranslations.If you ever want someone to lend an ear,: 話を聞いてほしくなったら、昼どきならいます。
exampleTranslations.Thanks for lending an ear last night. Th: 昨夜は話を聞いてくれてありがとう。それだけで十分でした。

nuanceJapanese: やや改まった温かい表現。相手は to で示し、助言ではなく聞くことに重点がある。

phrase: to cut a long story short
meaning: Used before you give only the main point of a long account.
easyEnglish: Used before you give only the main point of a long account.
japanese: 手短に言えば。かいつまんで言うと。
cue: A friend asks why you changed jobs. The full story is long.
reply: To cut a long story short, the team I joined for moved on.
transferCue: Summarise a complicated delay for a waiting colleague.
transferReply: To cut a long story short, the parts arrived at the wrong depot.
frame: To cut a long story short, …
nuance: Sits at the front of the sentence, followed by a comma. American English prefers to make a long story short.
aliases: to make a long story short

exampleTranslations.To cut a long story short, the team I jo: 手短に言うと、一緒に働きたかったチームがいなくなったんです。
exampleTranslations.To cut a long story short, the parts arr: かいつまんで言うと、部品が別の倉庫に届いてしまいました。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置き、コンマを続ける。アメリカ英語では to make a long story short を好む。

meaning: Accept part of what someone wants so you can agree.
easyEnglish: Accept part of what someone wants so you can agree.
japanese: 互いに歩み寄って折り合う。
cue: A supplier wants full payment upfront and you want none. Propose a compromise.
reply: Can we meet you halfway and pay half on signing?
transferCue: Resolve a disagreement about holiday dates with family.
transferReply: If you can start on the third, I'll meet you halfway on the return.
frame: Meet someone halfway on something
nuance: The person goes between meet and halfway. On introduces the point being settled.

exampleTranslations.Can we meet you halfway and pay half on: 歩み寄って、契約時に半額をお支払いするのはいかがでしょうか。
exampleTranslations.If you can start on the third, I'll meet: 3日から始められるなら、帰りの日程はこちらが歩み寄ります。

nuanceJapanese: 相手は meet と halfway のあいだに置く。折り合う内容は on で示す。

meaning: Fail to achieve the intended effect.
easyEnglish: Fail to achieve the intended effect.
japanese: ねらいどおりにならない。的を外す。
cue: A campaign was well made but did not reach its audience. Summarise.
reply: The design was strong, but the message missed the mark.
transferCue: Give honest feedback on a joke that did not land.
transferReply: The opening line missed the mark with that audience.
frame: Something misses the mark
nuance: The thing, not the person, is the subject. It judges effect rather than effort, which makes it usable in feedback.

exampleTranslations.The design was strong, but the message m: デザインはよかったのですが、伝えたいことが的を外していました。
exampleTranslations.The opening line missed the mark with th: 冒頭の一言は、あの聴衆には響きませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: 主語は人ではなく対象そのもの。努力ではなく結果を評価する言い方なので、フィードバックに使いやすい。

meaning: Achieve something that seemed impossible.
easyEnglish: Achieve something that seemed impossible.
japanese: 不可能に思えることを成し遂げる。
cue: A small team delivered something everyone thought was impossible. Praise them.
reply: They moved mountains to get it out by Friday.
transferCue: Describe what a parent did to support a child's education.
transferReply: She would move mountains for those two.
frame: Move mountains to do something
nuance: Always plural. Admiring rather than literal, often with would to describe willingness.

exampleTranslations.They moved mountains to get it out by Fr: 金曜に間に合わせるため、彼らは不可能を可能にしました。
あの二人のためなら、彼女はどんなことでもするでしょう。

nuanceJapanese: つねに複数形。文字どおりではなく称賛の表現で、would と組み合わせて意欲を表すことが多い。

meaning: Stop a problem while it is still small.
easyEnglish: Stop a problem while it is still small.
japanese: 問題が大きくなる前に、早めに摘み取る。
cue: Two team members have started avoiding each other. Suggest acting early.
reply: Let's nip it in the bud before it affects the handover.
transferCue: Describe how you stopped a habit from taking hold.
transferReply: I nipped it in the bud by deleting the app after one week.
frame: Nip something in the bud
nuance: The object goes between nip and in. It only works before the problem has grown, so timing is part of the meaning.

exampleTranslations.Let's nip it in the bud before it affect: 引き継ぎに影響する前に、早めに手を打ちましょう。
exampleTranslations.I nipped it in the bud by deleting the a: 1週間でアプリを消して、早いうちにやめました。

nuanceJapanese: 目的語は nip と in のあいだに置く。問題が育つ前にしか使えず、早さが意味の一部になっている。

meaning: Without preparation.
easyEnglish: Without preparation.
japanese: 準備なしで、その場で。
cue: You were asked to speak with no warning. Describe what you said.
reply: It was off the cuff, so I kept it to three points.
transferCue: Warn that an estimate is not yet reliable.
transferReply: That figure is off the cuff. Give me an hour and I'll check it.
frame: Be off the cuff / say something off the cuff
nuance: Used after be or a verb; off-the-cuff with hyphens before a noun. It excuses roughness without implying carelessness.

exampleTranslations.It was off the cuff, so I kept it to thr: 準備なしだったので、3点にしぼりました。
exampleTranslations.That figure is off the cuff. Give me an: その数字はその場で出したものです。1時間ください、確認します。

nuanceJapanese: be や動詞のあとに置き、名詞の前では off-the-cuff とハイフンでつなぐ。雑なのではなく、準備がなかったことを断る表現。

meaning: Doing something without thinking about it.
easyEnglish: Doing something without thinking about it.
japanese: 何も考えず、惰性で動いている。
cue: You drove to the office on a day you meant to go elsewhere. Explain.
reply: I was on autopilot and took the usual turning.
transferCue: Describe how a very busy week felt.
transferReply: I got through Thursday on autopilot and can't remember any of it.
frame: Be / do something on autopilot
nuance: Neutral about routine tasks, mildly negative about relationships or work that deserves attention.

exampleTranslations.I was on autopilot and took the usual tu: 何も考えずに、いつもの角を曲がってしまいました。
exampleTranslations.I got through Thursday on autopilot and: 木曜は惰性で乗り切って、ほとんど覚えていません。

nuanceJapanese: 日常の作業については中立だが、注意を要する仕事や人間関係について使うと否定的になる。

meaning: Forced to defend yourself rather than act.
easyEnglish: Forced to defend yourself rather than act.
japanese: 守勢に回って、後手に回る。

transferCue: Describe the first half of a difficult interview.
transferReply: I was on the back foot until they asked about the last project.
frame: Be / put someone on the back foot
nuance: British and often from sport. Put someone on the back foot names who caused it.

exampleTranslations.That announcement has put us on the back: あの発表で、こちらは後手に回りました。
exampleTranslations.I was on the back foot until they asked: 前回の案件の話が出るまで、ずっと受け身でした。

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語で、もとはスポーツの表現。put someone on the back foot と言えば、そうさせた側を示せる。

meaning: Cautious about repeating something that went badly before.
easyEnglish: Cautious about repeating something that went badly before.
japanese: 一度痛い目にあって、次は慎重になる。
cue: A friend asks why you read every clause of a contract now.
reply: Once bitten twice shy. The last one had a renewal clause I missed.
transferCue: Explain a colleague's reluctance to use a new supplier.
transferReply: She's once bitten twice shy after the delivery problems last year.
frame: Once bitten twice shy
nuance: A set proverb with no articles. Often stands alone as a full explanation.

exampleTranslations.Once bitten twice shy. The last one had: 一度痛い目にあったので慎重です。前回は更新条項を見落としました。
exampleTranslations.She's once bitten twice shy after the de: 去年の納品トラブルがあって、彼女は慎重になっています。

nuanceJapanese: 冠詞のない決まった形のことわざ。それだけで説明として完結することが多い。

meaning: Not like someone's usual behaviour.
easyEnglish: Not like someone's usual behaviour.
japanese: その人らしくない。

transferReply: Snapping like that was out of character, and I'm sorry.
frame: Be out of character for someone

exampleTranslations.That's out of character for him. I hope: 彼らしくありません。何もなければいいのですが。
exampleTranslations.Snapping like that was out of character,: あんなふうに声を荒らげたのは自分らしくなく、申し訳ありません。

nuanceJapanese: その人は for で示す。行為と人柄を切り離すので、気遣いながら指摘できる。

meaning: Too difficult for you to understand.
easyEnglish: Too difficult for you to understand.
japanese: 難しすぎて理解が追いつかない。

transferReply: Tell me if this goes over your head and I'll start again.

nuance: Usually with go and the information as subject. It can also mean a joke or hint was not noticed.

正直なところ、ほとんど理解が追いつきませんでした。
exampleTranslations.Tell me if this goes over your head and: 分かりにくければ言ってください。もう一度説明します。

nuanceJapanese: 描く対象は of で示す。paint a bleak picture のように形容詞を挟むと、その描写への評価を加えられる。

meaning: Be treated as less important than someone else.
easyEnglish: Be treated as less important than someone else.

exampleTranslations.She's tired of playing second fiddle on: 自分が設計した企画で、わき役扱いされることに彼女は疲れています。

nuanceJapanese: 目立つ側は to で示す。不満を含むことが多く、その立場をどう感じているかを伝える表現。

meaning: Go beyond the usual limits of what is done.
easyEnglish: Go beyond the usual limits of what is done.

exampleTranslations.They push the envelope every year, and a: 毎年、限界を押し広げようとしていて、半分くらいは形になります。

meaning: Rest, especially after working hard.
easyEnglish: Rest, especially after working hard.
japanese: 足を伸ばして、ゆっくり休む。

meaning: Cause surprise or mild disapproval.
easyEnglish: Cause surprise or mild disapproval.

easyEnglish: Perform well when a situation demands it.
japanese: ここぞという場面で、力を発揮する。

japanese: どうすればよいか分からず、困っている。
cue: A recurring fault has no obvious cause. Admit it honestly.
reply: I'm at a loss to explain why it only happens on Mondays.
transferCue: Describe your reaction to unexpectedly kind news.
transferReply: I was at a loss for words when they offered to help.
frame: Be at a loss to do something / for words
nuance: Followed by to plus a verb, or by for words. It admits difficulty without blaming anyone.

exampleTranslations.I'm at a loss to explain why it only hap: なぜ月曜だけ起きるのか、説明がつきません。
exampleTranslations.I was at a loss for words when they offe: 手伝うと言われたとき、言葉が出ませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: to＋動詞、または for words を続ける。誰も責めずに困惑を認める表現。

meaning: Whatever effort or sacrifice is needed.
easyEnglish: Whatever effort or sacrifice is needed.
japanese: どんな犠牲を払ってでも。
cue: One requirement cannot be compromised. State it clearly.
reply: We need to protect the delivery date at all costs.
transferCue: Describe a boundary you keep in your week.
transferReply: I protect Sunday mornings at all costs.
frame: Do something at all costs
nuance: Costs is always plural. Strong, so reserve it for genuine priorities or it loses force.

exampleTranslations.We need to protect the delivery date at: 納期だけは、何としても守る必要があります。
日曜の午前だけは、何があっても空けています。

nuanceJapanese: costs はつねに複数形。強い表現なので、本当に譲れないことに限らないと効果が薄れる。

meaning: At risk of being lost if things go wrong.
easyEnglish: At risk of being lost if things go wrong.
japanese: うまくいかなければ失われる、危うい状態にある。
cue: A decision affects the team's whole year. Explain the weight of it.
reply: There's a lot at stake, so let's take an extra day.
transferCue: Describe why a conversation felt difficult.
transferReply: Our friendship was at stake, which made it hard to be honest.
frame: Be at stake
nuance: The thing at risk is the subject. It raises the stakes of a discussion, so use it where the risk is real.

exampleTranslations.There's a lot at stake, so let's take an: 失うものが大きいので、もう1日かけましょう。
exampleTranslations.Our friendship was at stake, which made: 友情がかかっていたので、正直になるのが難しかったです。

nuanceJapanese: 危うくなっているものが主語になる。議論の重みを増す表現なので、実際に失うものがある場面で使う。

meaning: One immediately after another.
easyEnglish: One immediately after another.
japanese: 間を置かずに、続けて。
cue: Someone asks whether you have a free slot this afternoon.
reply: I'm back to back until four, sorry.
transferCue: Describe a busy weekend of events.
transferReply: We had two weddings back to back in June.
frame: Be back to back
nuance: Written back-to-back with hyphens before a noun. It describes scheduling, not physical position, in this sense.

すみません、4時まで予定が詰まっています。
exampleTranslations.We had two weddings back to back in June: 6月は結婚式が2件続けてありました。

nuanceJapanese: 名詞の前では back-to-back とハイフンでつなぐ。この意味では位置ではなく予定について使う。

meaning: Produce good results after a long time.
easyEnglish: Produce good results after a long time.
japanese: 時間をかけた努力が、実を結ぶ。
cue: A long outreach effort finally brought partners. Report it.
reply: Two years of visits have started to bear fruit.
transferCue: Describe a slow personal project.
transferReply: The garden is finally bearing fruit in its third year.
frame: Something bears fruit
nuance: Fruit stays singular and takes no article. It implies patience, so it suits slow results.

exampleTranslations.Two years of visits have started to bear: 2年にわたる訪問が、実を結び始めました。
exampleTranslations.The garden is finally bearing fruit in i: 庭は3年目にして、ようやく形になってきました。

nuanceJapanese: fruit は単数のままで冠詞は付かない。時間がかかることを含むので、ゆっくり出る成果に合う。

meaning: Politely disagree.
easyEnglish: Politely disagree.
japanese: 失礼ながら、意見が違うと述べる。
cue: A colleague says the old process was faster. Disagree politely.
reply: I beg to differ. The logs show it took two days longer.
transferCue: Disagree with a friend about a film.
transferReply: I beg to differ — the ending made the whole thing work.
frame: I beg to differ
nuance: Slightly formal and often lightly ironic. Usually a whole sentence, followed by your reason.

exampleTranslations.I beg to differ. The logs show it took t: 失礼ながら、意見が違います。記録では2日多くかかっています。
exampleTranslations.I beg to differ — the ending made the wh: 私は違う意見です。あの結末があってこそ、全体が生きています。

nuanceJapanese: やや改まった、軽い皮肉を含むことも多い表現。一文として使い、そのあとに理由を続ける。

meaning: Doing something late is better than not doing it.
easyEnglish: Doing something late is better than not doing it.
japanese: 遅くなっても、やらないよりはましだ。
cue: A friend apologises for a birthday message a week late.
reply: Better late than never. Thank you.
transferCue: Comment on starting a new skill in your forties.
transferReply: I started at forty-two, but better late than never.
frame: Better late than never
nuance: A set phrase, usually forgiving. Said about someone else's lateness it can sound pointed.

遅くても嬉しいです。ありがとう。
exampleTranslations.I started at forty-two, but better late: 42歳で始めましたが、やらないよりずっといいです。

nuanceJapanese: 決まった言い回しで、ふつうは相手を許す響き。他人の遅れについて言うと、とげを含むことがある。

meaning: It is wiser to be careful than to risk regret.
easyEnglish: It is wiser to be careful than to risk regret.
japanese: あとで後悔するより、用心したほうがいい。
cue: A friend thinks a second copy of the documents is excessive.
reply: Better safe than sorry. Print one for your bag.
transferCue: Explain why you left early for an appointment.
transferReply: I left an hour early — better safe than sorry.
frame: Better safe than sorry
nuance: A set phrase justifying caution. It works best with the specific precaution you are suggesting.

exampleTranslations.Better safe than sorry. Print one for yo: 用心するに越したことはありません。かばん用に1部印刷しましょう。
exampleTranslations.I left an hour early — better safe than: 1時間早く出ました。用心しておくに越したことはありません。

nuanceJapanese: 用心を正当化する決まった言い回し。具体的な対策を添えると効果的。

meaning: Wait patiently for the right moment.
easyEnglish: Wait patiently for the right moment.
japanese: 好機を待って、じっと構える。
cue: A colleague wants to raise a proposal during a tense week. Advise waiting.
reply: Bide your time until the review is over.
transferCue: Describe how you handled a slow market.
transferReply: We bided our time and bought in the autumn.
frame: Bide your time
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Bide is used almost only in this phrase.

評価が終わるまで、時機を待ちましょう。
exampleTranslations.We bided our time and bought in the autu: 時機を待って、秋に購入しました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。bide はほぼこの表現でしか使われない。

meaning: Be the first to do something that others then follow.
easyEnglish: Be the first to do something that others then follow.
japanese: 先駆けとなって、道を切り開く。
cue: A team's method has been copied across the company. Recognise it.
reply: Your team blazed a trail with the shared checklist.
transferCue: Describe an early figure in a field.
transferReply: She blazed a trail for women in structural engineering.
frame: Blaze a trail for someone
nuance: For introduces who follows. Admiring, and often used about people who went first in difficult conditions.

exampleTranslations.Your team blazed a trail with the shared: 共有のチェックリストで、あなたのチームが道を切り開きました。
exampleTranslations.She blazed a trail for women in structur: 彼女は構造工学の分野で、女性の道を切り開きました。

nuanceJapanese: 続く人は for で示す。称賛の表現で、困難な状況で先陣を切った人について使うことが多い。

meaning: Suddenly become very angry.
easyEnglish: Suddenly become very angry.
japanese: かんしゃくを起こす。
cue: You reacted badly to a repeated mistake. Reflect on it.
reply: I blew my top over the third missed deadline, which didn't help.
transferCue: Warn a colleague how a client may react.
transferReply: He might blow his top when he sees the invoice.
frame: Blow your top
nuance: Informal, and the possessive follows the subject. It describes a sudden outburst rather than lasting anger.

exampleTranslations.I blew my top over the third missed dead: 3度目の締め切り超過でかんしゃくを起こしてしまい、逆効果でした。
exampleTranslations.He might blow his top when he sees the i: 請求書を見たら、彼は怒り出すかもしれません。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現で、所有格は主語に合わせる。続く怒りではなく、突発的な爆発を指す。

meaning: Tell someone about something important, often bad.
easyEnglish: Tell someone about something important, often bad.
japanese: 重要な知らせを、本人に伝える。
cue: A decision affects a colleague who has not heard yet. Offer to tell them.
reply: I'll break the news to her before the meeting.
transferCue: Describe telling a family member about a move.
transferReply: We broke the news over dinner so everyone heard it together.
frame: Break the news to someone
nuance: To introduces the person told. It implies care about how the news lands, not just informing.

exampleTranslations.I'll break the news to her before the me: 会議の前に、私から彼女に伝えます。
exampleTranslations.We broke the news over dinner so everyon: みんなが同時に聞けるよう、夕食の席で伝えました。

nuanceJapanese: 伝える相手は to で示す。単なる伝達ではなく、受け止め方への配慮を含む。

meaning: Do something that makes people notice and remember you.
easyEnglish: Do something that makes people notice and remember you.
japanese: 存在を認められる成果を残す。
cue: A new colleague asks how to build a reputation in the team.
reply: You'll make your mark faster by finishing one thing well than by starting five.
transferCue: Describe an artist's first exhibition.
transferReply: She made her mark with a single room of small drawings.
frame: Make your mark on something
nuance: The possessive follows the subject and on introduces the field. It is about recognition, not about winning.

exampleTranslations.You'll make your mark faster by finishin: 5つ始めるより、1つをきちんと仕上げたほうが早く認められます。
exampleTranslations.She made her mark with a single room of: 彼女は小さな素描だけの一室で、確かな印象を残しました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせ、分野は on で示す。勝つことではなく、認められることを表す。

meaning: Encounter someone as strong or skilled as you.
easyEnglish: Encounter someone as strong or skilled as you.
japanese: 自分に匹敵する相手に出会う。
cue: A famously fast colleague was outpaced by a newcomer. Comment.
reply: He's finally met his match on the crossword.
transferCue: Describe a close game between two strong teams.
transferReply: They met their match in the semi-final.
frame: Meet your match
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Usually admiring and light, not a warning.

exampleTranslations.He's finally met his match on the crossw: クロスワードで、彼もついに好敵手に出会いました。
準決勝で、彼らは互角の相手に当たりました。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。警告ではなく、感心を込めた軽い表現。

meaning: Notice every detail and every opportunity.
easyEnglish: Notice every detail and every opportunity.
japanese: 細かい点も好機も、決して見逃さない。
cue: A colleague spotted an error nobody else saw. Praise them.
reply: You don't miss a trick. That was on page eleven.
transferCue: Describe a shopkeeper who remembers every customer.
transferReply: He doesn't miss a trick — he knew I'd been away.
frame: Not miss a trick
nuance: Almost always negative in form but complimentary in meaning. Trick stays singular.

exampleTranslations.You don't miss a trick. That was on page: 本当によく見ていますね。11ページの話です。
exampleTranslations.He doesn't miss a trick — he knew I'd be: 彼は何も見逃しません。私が留守にしていたことも知っていました。

nuanceJapanese: 形はほぼつねに否定だが、意味はほめ言葉。trick は単数のまま。

meaning: People with money get what they want.
easyEnglish: People with money get what they want.
japanese: 金がものを言う。
cue: A late application was accepted after a large donation. Comment drily.
reply: Money talks, apparently.
transferCue: Explain how one bidder won a contested sale.
transferReply: Three of us wanted the flat, but money talks.
frame: Money talks
nuance: A set saying, usually critical. Money is the subject and takes no article.

やはり、金がものを言うということですね。
exampleTranslations.Three of us wanted the flat, but money t: 3人が欲しがった部屋でしたが、結局は金がものを言いました。

nuanceJapanese: 決まった言い回しで、ふつうは批判的。主語は money で冠詞は付かない。

meaning: Usually; most of the time.
easyEnglish: Usually; most of the time.
japanese: たいていの場合は。
cue: A friend asks whether the bus is reliable.
reply: More often than not it's on time, but leave a margin.
transferCue: Describe a pattern you have noticed at work.
transferReply: More often than not, the problem is the input file.
frame: More often than not, …
nuance: Usually opens a sentence with a comma. It claims a tendency, not a rule, so it is a careful way to generalise.

exampleTranslations.More often than not it's on time, but le: たいていは時間どおりですが、余裕は見ておいてください。
exampleTranslations.More often than not, the problem is the: たいていの場合、原因は入力ファイルです。

nuanceJapanese: 文頭に置いてコンマを続けるのがふつう。規則ではなく傾向を述べるので、慎重に一般化できる。

meaning: Exactly level in a competition.
easyEnglish: Exactly level in a competition.
japanese: 競り合って、互角である。
cue: Two candidates scored almost identically. Describe the position.
reply: They're neck and neck after the second round.
transferCue: Describe two products competing in a market.
transferReply: The two brands have been neck and neck all year.
frame: Be neck and neck with someone
nuance: From horse racing. With introduces the rival, and it describes an ongoing contest rather than a result.

exampleTranslations.They're neck and neck after the second r: 2回戦を終えて、二人は互角です。
exampleTranslations.The two brands have been neck and neck a: その2ブランドは、一年中競り合っています。

nuanceJapanese: 競馬に由来する。競争相手は with で示し、結果ではなく進行中の接戦を表す。

meaning: Two people clearly dislike each other.
easyEnglish: Two people clearly dislike each other.
japanese: 互いに好意を持っていない。
cue: Two colleagues avoid each other's meetings. Describe it discreetly.
reply: There's no love lost between those two.
transferCue: Explain why you seated two guests apart.
transferReply: There's no love lost there, so I split the table.
frame: There's no love lost between X and Y
nuance: Almost always with there's and between. An understatement: it means real dislike.

あの二人のあいだには、好意はありません。
exampleTranslations.There's no love lost there, so I split t: 折り合いがよくないので、席を離しました。

nuanceJapanese: ほぼつねに there's と between を伴う。控えめな言い方で、実際にははっきりした反感を意味する。

meaning: Know nothing at all about something.
easyEnglish: Know nothing at all about something.

transferCue: Describe your first day in a new role.
transferReply: On day one I didn't have a clue where anything was.
frame: Not have a clue about something
nuance: Informal. About someone else it sounds dismissive; about yourself it is ordinary honesty.

exampleTranslations.I don't have a clue how that one works,: 申し訳ありませんが、それの仕組みはまったく分かりません。
exampleTranslations.On day one I didn't have a clue where an: 初日は、何がどこにあるのかまるで分かりませんでした。

nuanceJapanese: くだけた表現。他人について言うと見下す響きになるが、自分のことならふつうの率直な言い方。

meaning: Because you chose to, without being asked.
easyEnglish: Because you chose to, without being asked.
japanese: 言われたからではなく、自分の意思で。

transferCue: Describe why a child started helping at home.
transferReply: He started clearing the table of his own accord.
frame: Do something of your own accord
nuance: The possessive follows the subject. Slightly formal, and it emphasises that nobody asked.

exampleTranslations.She did it of her own accord, which made: 彼女は自分から取り組んだので、なおさら見事でした。

nuanceJapanese: 所有格は主語に合わせる。やや改まった表現で、誰にも頼まれていないことを強調する。

meaning: At the same level or quality as something else.

nuanceJapanese: イギリス英語では thoughts と複数形、アメリカ英語では on second thought。文頭に置き、考えを変えたことを示す。
